after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that $a\cdot b=-8$, find the angle between $a=⟨2t,2t⟩$ and $b=⟨4,-2⟩.$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
after.worked_solution:
First, since $a\cdot b=-8$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-8 \\ 2t\cdot 4+2t\cdot (-2) & =-8 \\ 8t-4t & =-8 \\ 4t & =-8 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨2(-2),\,2(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-8}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{8}{4\sqrt{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{5}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}})≈{108.4}^{∘}.
$$

First, since a⋅b=−8, we can solve for t, as follows:

a⋅b=−82t⋅4+2t⋅(−2)=−88t−4t=−84t=−8t=−2

So, a=⟨2(−2),2(−2)⟩=⟨−4,−4⟩.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(−110)≈108.4∘.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}x=⟨-1,0,3⟩,\,y=⟨-2,2,3⟩,\,z=⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△XYZ$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠XZY=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038738/assets/87453fecb9da6b9e673ab5a85a289a3fac73f4fb90fc8f1b33e7c0a80b1ea77f.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ZX} & =x-z \\  & =⟨-1,0,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{ZY} & =y-z \\  & =⟨-2,2,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{ZX}\cdot \overset{\to }{ZY}}{|\overset{\to }{ZX}||\overset{\to }{ZY}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0+1\cdot 3+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={45}^{∘}.
$$

Find ∠XZY given the points X(−1,0,3), Y(−2,2,3), and Z(−2,−1,3).

a

b

EXPLANATION

Note that the position vectors of the points X, Y, Z are

x=⟨−1,0,3⟩,y=⟨−2,2,3⟩,z=⟨−2,−1,3⟩.

The △XYZ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote ∠XZY=θ.

First, we find the components of ZX→ and ZY→: ZX→=x−z=⟨−1,0,3⟩−⟨−2,−1,3⟩=⟨1,1,0⟩ZY→=y−z=⟨−2,2,3⟩−⟨−2,−1,3⟩=⟨0,3,0⟩

Now, the cosine of the angle between ZX→ and ZY→ is

cos⁡θ=ZX→⋅ZY→|ZX→||ZY→|=1⋅0+1⋅3+0⋅012+12+0202+32+02=32⋅9=12.

Therefore, θ=arccos⁡(12)=45∘.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
content.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}x=⟨-1,0,3⟩,\,y=⟨-2,2,3⟩,\,z=⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△XYZ$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠XZY=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14038738/assets/87453fecb9da6b9e673ab5a85a289a3fac73f4fb90fc8f1b33e7c0a80b1ea77f.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ZX} & =x-z \\  & =⟨-1,0,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{ZY} & =y-z \\  & =⟨-2,2,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{ZX}\cdot \overset{\to }{ZY}}{|\overset{\to }{ZX}||\overset{\to }{ZY}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0+1\cdot 3+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={45}^{∘}.
$$
